2609.30243.title: JevOut: Natural Context Can Flip Decision Models
2609.30243.paper_summary: Dedicated decision models such as Jev map unstructured language to probability distributions over finite choices, allowing their outputs to directly route requests, select tools, and trigger actions. Yet real-world inputs rarely arrive in isolation: they come with background details and surrounding context. We find that short additions that fit naturally into this context can nevertheless redirect an otherwise correct decision, even when the correct answer remains unchanged. To study this behavior, we fix a wrong target option for each initially correct item and use the model's option probabilities to refine fluent context additions while preserving the source, question, choices, and gold answer. Within 64 accepted target evaluations, the optimizer identifies contexts that redirect Jev on 312 of 508 initially correct decisions (61.4%); in 229 cases, Jev assigns at least 0.7 probability to the fixed wrong option. Across seven datasets, three additional decision systems show targeted flip rates of 64.9%-73.2% on decisions they initially answer correctly. Taken together, these results expose a pronounced fragility in current decision models: short, ordinary-looking context can shift a correct choice to a high-confidence wrong one. Because these models turn language directly into downstream choices, this sensitivity raises concerns about treating their probability outputs as reliable decision interfaces.
2609.30243.paper_summary_zh: 專門的決策模型如Jev將非結構化語言映射到有限選擇上的概率分佈，使其輸出能夠直接路由請求、選擇工具和觸發行動。然實際世界中的輸入很少是孤立到達的：它們伴隨著背景細節和周圍的上下文。我們發現，適合自然融入這種上下文的短小補充，仍然可以重新引導一個原本正確的決策，即使正確答案保持不變。為了研究這種行為，我們為每個最初正確的項目固定一個錯誤的目標選項，並利用模型的選項概率來精煉流暢的上下文補充，同時保留來源、問題、選擇和正確答案。在64個接受的目標評估中，優化器識別出能夠重新引導Jev的上下文，涉及508個最初正確的決策中的312個（61.4%）；在229個案例中，Jev對固定的錯誤選項賦予至少0.7的概率。在七個數據集上，另外三個決策系統在最初正確回答的決策上顯示出64.9%-73.2%的目標翻轉率。綜合這些結果，揭示了當前決策模型中明顯的脆弱性：短小、看似普通的上下文可以將正確選擇轉變為高置信度的錯誤選擇。由於這些模型將語言直接轉化為下游選擇，這種敏感性引發了將其概率輸出視為可靠決策界面的擔憂。
2609.30243.author: Zixiang Xu et.al.
